title: Warrior's Path
hint: Hint: Read the key concepts of this module carefully to find the correct answer.
exitModalText: If you leave now, you'll lose your progress for this level and the chance to earn points.
noLivesText: You're out of lives. Go back to the map and try again.
level1Title: The Lost Key of the Pancreas
answerGuide: Write the number of the correct answer:
l1_q1_enun: What is the main function of insulin in our body?
l1_q1_op0: It's the fuel that makes us hungry.
l1_q1_op1: It's the "key" that allows glucose to enter cells to give us energy.
l1_q1_op2: It's a type of sugar floating in the blood.
l1_q1_op3: It's a hormone the stomach makes to digest water.
l1_q1_ok: Correct! Insulin acts like a key opening cell doors so glucose can enter and become energy.
l1_q1_bad: Try again! Glucose is fuel and insulin is the key that opens the cell door.
l1_q2_enun: True or False? Having Type 1 Diabetes means you made a mistake in your diet or ate too many sweets.
l1_q2_ok: Exactly! Type 1 Diabetes is not caused by sweets or anything you did wrong.
l1_q2_bad: Don't worry! It's a common myth. Type 1 is not your fault; the pancreas stopped making insulin.
l1_q3_enun: Your friend asks why you need insulin before eating. What empowering answer would you give?
l1_q3_op0: "Because I'm punished and can't eat normally."
l1_q3_op1: "Because insulin is the key that gives my body energy to play and explore with you."
l1_q3_op2: "Because insulin makes glucose disappear from my body forever."
l1_q3_ok: Great answer! Insulin gives your body the key to turn food into energy.
l1_q3_bad: Close! Diabetes isn't a punishment; insulin helps turn food into energy.
l1_q4_enun: When glucose can't enter cells due to lack of insulin keys, what signs can the body show? (Select all correct)
l1_q4_op0: Excessive thirst and drinking water often.
l1_q4_ok: Excellent! Thirst, frequent urination and fatigue are signs when glucose can't enter cells.
l1_q4_bad: Check again! Superpowers aren't a sign. Excess glucose is eliminated in urine causing thirst and fatigue.
l2_q1_enun: Why wash hands with soap and water and dry completely before using a glucose meter?
l2_q1_op0: To turn the meter on faster.
l2_q1_op1: Food, sugar or moisture on fingers can affect the glucose reading.
l2_q1_op3: To prevent the meter button from sticking.
l2_q1_ok: Correct! Clean, dry hands ensure an accurate reading.
l2_q1_bad: Try again! Residue on fingers can change the glucose value.
l2_q2_enun: True or False? The best spot is the center of the fingertip and you should reuse the same lancet several times.
l2_q2_ok: Excellent! Prick the sides of the fingertip and use a new lancet each time.
l2_q2_bad: Review technique! Center pricks hurt more and reusing lancets increases risk.
l2_q3_enun: Applying a new CGM sensor. Which action is correct?
l2_q3_op0: Apply lotion or oil just before sticking it.
l2_q3_op1: Wash the area with soap and water, make sure skin is clean and completely dry.
l2_q3_op2: Blow on damp skin to dry quickly.
l2_q3_ok: Perfect! Clean, dry skin helps the adhesive stick properly.
l2_q3_bad: Careful! Lotions or moisture prevent proper adhesion.
l2_q4_enun: Which statements about CGM are correct? (Select all)
l2_q4_op0: It measures glucose continuously in fluid under the skin.
l2_q4_op1: It sends data to a compatible app or receiver.
l2_q4_op2: It must be applied to clean, dry skin.
l2_q4_op3: It replaces insulin or a balanced diet.
l2_q4_ok: Great selection! Measures, sends data, needs clean dry skin.
l2_q4_bad: Review! CGM doesn't replace insulin or a balanced diet.
l3_q1_enun: According to guidelines, what's the target glucose range before meals?
l3_q1_ok: Exactly! 70-130 mg/dL before meals is the target range.
l3_q1_bad: Try again! Target before meals is 70-130 mg/dL.
l3_q2_enun: True or False? Hypoglycemia is when glucose is below 70 mg/dL.
l3_q2_ok: Correct! Below 70 mg/dL is considered hypoglycemia.
l3_q3_enun: Playing and your meter shows 62 mg/dL with dizziness and sweating. What's correct?
l3_q3_op1: Tell an adult, pause, and take fast-acting carbs.
l3_q3_op2: Go to sleep without telling anyone.
l3_q3_ok: Perfect decision! Pause, tell an adult, take fast-acting sugar.
l3_q3_bad: Be careful! Pause, tell adult, take fast-acting carbs.
l3_q4_enun: When should you check glucose? (Select all)
l3_q4_ok: Perfect score! All are key times to check.
l3_q4_bad: Review! These are all recommended times.
l4_q1_enun: What is hypoglycemia and below what number is it low?
l4_q1_op2: When pancreas makes too many insulin keys
l4_q1_ok: Excellent! Hypoglycemia is glucose below 70 mg/dL.
l4_q1_bad: Try again! Alert is below 70 mg/dL.
l4_q2_enun: True or False? Chocolate or candy with nuts are perfect for quickly raising glucose.
l4_q2_ok: Correct! Fat slows absorption. Use fast-acting carbs without fat.
l4_q2_bad: Watch out! Fat delays sugar absorption.
l4_q3_enun: With 62 mg/dL and symptoms, using Rule of 15, what do you do?
l4_q3_op2: Take 15g fast-acting carb, wait 15 min, recheck
l4_q4_enun: Which are real hypoglycemia symptoms? (Select correct ones)
l4_q4_ok: Great! Shakiness, cold sweats, hunger and irritability are low symptoms.
l4_q4_bad: Watch! Thirst/urination are high glucose symptoms.
l5_q1_op3: Excess glucose in blood due to lack of insulin or it didn't work in time
l5_q1_ok: Exactly! Excess glucose due to insufficient insulin.
l5_q1_bad: Review! Hyperglycemia is excess glucose from lack of insulin.
l5_q2_enun: True or False? Drinking water during hyperglycemia helps hydration and removes excess glucose via kidneys.
l5_q2_ok: Correct! Water helps prevent dehydration and process excess sugar.
l5_q2_bad: It's True! Water helps during hyperglycemia.
l5_q3_enun: With 230 mg/dL, thirst and blurry vision, what's the right action?
l5_q3_op0: Tell adult, drink water, take correction insulin as directed
l5_q3_op2: Run at full speed without telling adult
l5_q3_op3: Put meter away and don't check until tomorrow
l5_q3_ok: Perfect! Tell adult, hydrate, follow medical plan.
l5_q3_bad: Remember protocol! With high glucose tell adult, hydrate, use correction.
l5_q4_op1: Cold sweats, shakiness and sudden dizziness
l5_q4_ok: Great! Thirst, frequent urination, fatigue and blurry vision are high glucose signs.
l5_q4_bad: Review! Shakiness/cold sweats are low glucose symptoms.
l6_q1_enun: What are ketones and why does the body produce them?
l6_q1_op1: Acids produced when body burns fat for fuel due to lack of insulin
l6_q1_ok: Detective work! Ketones form when cells can't use glucose and burn fat.
l6_q1_bad: Adjust lens! Without insulin, body burns fat producing ketones.
l6_q2_enun: True or False? Ketones should only be checked when glucose is very low.
l6_q2_ok: Correct! False. Check ketones when glucose ≥250 mg/dL or when sick.
l6_q2_bad: Careful! Check when high or when unwell.
l6_q3_enun: With 260 mg/dL, nausea and feeling ill, what's immediate action?
l6_q3_op0: Drink soda and go to sleep
l6_q3_op3: Tell adult, check ketones, hydrate, follow correction plan
l6_q3_ok: Excellent protocol! Tell adult, check ketones, hydrate, correct insulin.
l6_q3_bad: Never stop insulin! Check ketones, hydrate, use correction.
l6_q4_op0: Never skip or stop prescribed insulin
l6_q4_op1: Check ketones if glucose ≥250 mg/dL or sick
l6_q4_op3: Stay hydrated and seek care if vomiting persistently
l6_q4_ok: Well done! Keep insulin, check ketones, hydrate.
l6_q4_bad: Hydration matters! Don't stop water, don't skip insulin.
l7_q1_op3: Carbs turn into glucose and raise blood sugar after eating
l7_q1_ok: Great! Carbs are the main nutrient converted to glucose.
l7_q1_bad: Try again! Carbs break down to glucose after eating.
l7_q2_enun: True or False? Grilled chicken, egg and olive oil raise glucose immediately.
l7_q2_ok: Correct! Protein and fat have little direct carb impact.
l7_q2_bad: Meat, eggs, oils have no carbs, so minimal immediate effect.
l7_q3_enun: Meal: chicken, salad, 1/3 cup cooked rice, water. What to count?
l7_q3_ok: Explorer choice! Rice is the carb source to count.
l7_q3_bad: Check! Rice is the carb-containing food.
l7_q4_enun: Which groups contain carbs to count? (Select correct)
l7_q4_op2: Grains and starchy veggies (bread, pasta, rice, oats, potatoes)
l7_q4_ok: Perfect! Fruit, dairy, grains and starchy veggies have carbs.
l7_q4_bad: Note! Meat, fish, eggs, oils have no carbs.
l8_q1_enun: When reading nutrition label, what to look at first?
l8_q1_op2: Serving size to know what amounts the values refer to
l8_q1_ok: Label master! Carbs are for that specific serving size.
l8_q2_enun: True or False? Weighing food is more accurate than eyeballing.
l8_q2_ok: Excellent! Digital scale is most precise.
l8_q2_bad: Eyeballing often under/overestimates. Weighing is more accurate.
l8_q3_enun: Without scale, what equals 1/2 cup cooked pasta?
l8_q3_op2: Two hands open forming a bowl
l8_q3_ok: Great! Closed fist equals ~1/2 cup of grains/pasta.
l8_q4_enun: Correct steps for carb counting? (Select correct)
l8_q4_op0: Find serving size and total carbs
l8_q4_op2: Subtract protein and fat from carbs
l8_q4_op3: Calculate proportional carbs based on weight served
l9_q1_op1: Inject rapid insulin 15-20 minutes BEFORE first bite
l9_q2_enun: True or False? Pre-bolus helps match insulin to carb absorption and prevents post-meal spikes.
l9_q2_bad: Yes, true. Without pre-bolus carbs enter before insulin works.
l9_q3_enun: With glucose 65 mg/dL before meal, what's correct?
l9_q3_op0: Inject insulin and wait without eating
l9_q3_op3: Treat low to ≥70 mg/dL first, then adjust insulin timing with care team
l9_q3_ok: Safe strategy! Treat low first, then dose for meal.
l9_q3_bad: Never pre-bolus when low! Treat first to safe range.
l9_q4_op1: Low starting glucose or high-fat meal that digests slowly
l9_q4_ok: Pay attention! Low glucose or fatty meal affects timing.
l9_q4_bad: Only biological factors affect pre-bolus timing.
l10_q1_enun: What's the main role of basal insulin?
l10_q1_op1: Provides steady insulin to keep glucose stable between meals and overnight
l10_q1_bad: Basal is background insulin between meals and at night.
l10_q2_enun: True or False? Bolus insulin is used to maintain glucose overnight.
l10_q2_ok: Perfect! False. Bolus is for meals/corrections; basal is overnight/daytime background.
l10_q2_bad: Basal works overnight, bolus is for food/corrections.
l10_q3_enun: With 210 mg/dL about to eat pasta, which insulin?
l10_q3_op2: Rapid/ultra-rapid bolus to cover carbs and correct
l10_q3_ok: Masterful! Bolus covers meal and correction.
l10_q3_bad: With meal and high glucose you need bolus.
l10_q4_op0: Basal usually given at fixed time daily
l10_q4_op2: Bolus starts working in ~15 min for meals
l10_q4_ok: Great! Basal fixed, bolus fast for meals.
l10_q4_bad: Bolus not weekly and doesn't raise glucose. Basal is fixed.
l11_q1_enun: Why prime/purge pen (2 units) before injecting?
l11_q1_op2: To remove air bubbles and ensure flow for accurate dose
l11_q1_ok: Artist technique! Removes air bubbles for exact dose.
l11_q1_bad: Air bubbles can steal units. Priming ensures accuracy.
l11_q2_enun: True or False? Remove needle immediately after pressing button.
l11_q2_ok: Correct! Count 10 seconds before removing needle.
l11_q3_enun: After pressing button fully, what before removing needle?
l11_q3_op0: Rub in circles while needle inside
l11_q3_op1: Keep button pressed and count to 10
l11_q3_op2: Release button hard and pull quickly
l11_q3_ok: Perfect! Counting 10 seconds ensures full dose absorbed.
l11_q3_bad: Press, count to 10, then remove gently.
l11_q4_op0: Clean hands, new needle each time
l11_q4_op1: Prime with 2 units pointing up until drop appears
l11_q4_ok: Complete checklist! Clean, prime, new needle, correct injection.
l11_q4_bad: Never reuse needles. One use = new needle.
l12_q1_op1: Lumps/hard fat from injecting same spot repeatedly, causing unpredictable absorption
l12_q1_ok: Badge earned! Lumps prevent proper insulin absorption.
l12_q1_bad: Repeated same site creates lumps affecting absorption.
l12_q2_enun: True or False? Injecting same spot every time is best for consistent absorption.
l12_q2_ok: Perfect! False. Rotate, move at least 1-2 cm from previous spot.
l12_q3_enun: You feel a hard lump before injecting. What to do?
l12_q3_op2: Use healthy skin site, rest lump, tell care team
l12_q3_ok: Correct protection! Use healthy skin for proper absorption.
l12_q3_bad: Never inject into lipodystrophy. Use healthy skin.
l12_q4_enun: Which are approved injection sites? (Select correct)
l12_q4_op3: Back of upper arm and outer upper buttocks
l12_q4_ok: Map complete! Abdomen, thighs, arms, buttocks.
l12_q4_bad: Joints and palms not approved sites.
l13_q1_enun: What happens to glucose during exercise?
l13_q1_op0: Exercise blocks insulin and always raises glucose
l13_q1_op2: Increases insulin sensitivity, muscles use glucose - may drop during and up to 24-48h after
l13_q1_ok: Athlete answer! Exercise uses glucose and increases insulin sensitivity.
l13_q1_bad: Drops can happen during or up to 24-48h after exercise.
l13_q2_enun: True or False? For training you only need shoes.
l13_q2_ok: Great prevention! Check glucose before and bring fast-acting carbs.
l13_q2_bad: Always check before and pack fast carbs for lows.
l13_q3_enun: Before intense soccer, glucose 90 mg/dL with down arrow. What's correct?
l13_q3_op0: Have carb snack, tell coach, keep fast carbs nearby
l13_q3_op3: Drink caffeinated soda and play without rechecking
l13_q3_ok: Perfect strategy! Prevent with carbs and communication.
l13_q3_bad: With down arrow at 90, eat carbs before exercise.
l13_q4_op3: Triple bolus before running without eating
l13_q4_ok: Ready! Check and carry fast carbs.
l13_q4_bad: Stay hydrated, don't overbolus without food.
l14_q1_enun: Sick with fever/little appetite. Golden rule?
l14_q1_op3: NEVER stop insulin; adjust with medical guidance
l14_q1_ok: Golden rule! Body needs insulin when sick; hormones can raise glucose.
l14_q1_bad: Stopping insulin when sick is dangerous - can cause DKA.
l14_q2_enun: True or False? Teachers and trusted friends should know about your Type 1 Diabetes.
l14_q2_ok: True! Social support helps in emergencies.
l14_q2_bad: Telling trusted people lets them help quickly.
l14_q3_enun: In exam feeling cold sweat, dizzy, shaky. What to do?
l14_q3_op1: Tell teacher, check glucose, take fast-acting carbs
l14_q3_op3: Ask for candy and pocket it without eating
l14_q3_bad: Never stay silent - treat low immediately.
l14_q4_enun: When sick, what to do? (Select correct)
l14_q4_op1: Check glucose more often, check ketones if >250 mg/dL
l14_q4_op3: Give soft/liquid carbs if can't eat solids
l14_q4_ok: Great! Hydrate, monitor, provide carbs as needed.
l15_q1_enun: What is glucagon and when to use?
l15_q1_op1: Fast-acting hormone for severe lows when unconscious or can't swallow
l15_q1_ok: Rescue knowledge! Glucagon tells liver to release glucose in emergencies.
l15_q1_bad: Glucagon is emergency med, not insulin.
l15_q2_enun: True or False? Glucagon kit should be locked away secretly.
l15_q2_ok: Correct! Must be accessible to family, teachers, caregivers.
l15_q2_bad: Quick access saves lives - everyone should know location/use.
l15_q3_enun: Person unconscious from severe low. What's procedure?
l15_q3_op1: Sit in chair and wait 2 hours
l15_q3_op2: Give glucagon (nasal/injectable), place on side, call emergency services
l15_q3_op3: Inject double rapid insulin and ice forehead
l15_q3_ok: Correct protocol! Glucagon, recovery position, call EMS.
l15_q3_bad: Never put food/drink in unconscious person.
l15_q4_enun: What message sums up living with Type 1? (Select correct)
l15_q4_op1: Not a limit or punishment - with knowledge, monitoring, prep you can reach any goal
l15_q4_op2: Must isolate from friends and skip trips
l15_q4_op3: Monitoring decides if you're good or bad person
l15_q4_ok: Gold graduate! Diabetes doesn't limit you - you can achieve any dream.
l15_q4_bad: Diabetes doesn't define or limit you!
